newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices firm on shortage of stocks.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices firm on shortage of stocks.

text.p: Cotton prices were steady to firm on Monday due to a shortfall in the availability of quality stock as the current season neared its end, dealers said.
"There's a scarcity of quality cottons," said a leading trader. "There's not much stock around."
Traders said most of the crop from the 1996/97 cotton season (October/September), estimated at a record 16.78 million bales (one bale is 170 kg), had arrived in the market.
They said farmers were now getting ready for sowing operations with monsoon rains anticipated in the second week of June.
In spot, Bengal-deshi was quoted at 1,010/1,030 rupees per maund (37.32 kg). F-414 rose 50 rupees to 2,110 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose 200 rupees to 14,500/14,700 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
